papers.title: Conformal k-NN Anomaly Detector for Univariate Data Streams
papers.abstract: Anomalies in time-series data give essential and often actionable information in many applications. In this paper we consider a model-free anomaly detection method for univariate time-series which adapts to non-stationarity in the data stream and provides probabilistic abnormality scores based on the conformal prediction paradigm. Despite its simplicity the method performs on par with complex prediction-based models on the Numenta Anomaly Detection benchmark and the Yahoo! S5 dataset.

summary_en.motivation: To develop a model-free anomaly detection method for univariate data streams that adapts to non-stationarity and provides probabilistic scores.
summary_en.method: A conformal prediction framework using k-nearest neighbors to compute anomaly scores without requiring a predictive model.
summary_en.result: The method achieves competitive performance on the Numenta and Yahoo S5 benchmarks compared to complex prediction-based approaches.
summary_en.validation: Validated on two standard time-series anomaly detection benchmarks (Numenta and Yahoo S5).
